interest: This file is exceptionally valuable to diplomatic, economic, and intelligence historians studying the run-up to the Pacific War. It provides a granular chronological index of the rapid transition from routine exchange control friction to full-scale economic warfare between the United States and Japan between 1940 and early 1942. The purports illustrate the practical impact of financial controls on major American multinational corporations—such as The Paraffine Companies and Eastman Kodak—that faced forced divestiture, blocked remittances, and 'Japanization' of corporate equity. Furthermore, the file sheds light on Japan's international strategies to circumvent dollar shortages and U.S. sanctions through triangular trade, bullion shipments, and banking arrangements in Latin America (Peru, Brazil, Bolivia, and Chile) and Southeast Asia (French Indochina and the Netherlands East Indies), alongside counter-intelligence monitoring by the FBI and the Coordinator of Information.
overview: File 894.5151 (File 33) consists of the Department of State's docket list of papers recording incoming and outgoing telegrams, despatches, memoranda, and correspondence concerning Japanese foreign exchange and monetary conditions from January 1940 to March 1942. The records document the progressive tightening of Japanese foreign exchange control laws, currency concentration systems, and the severe difficulties encountered by American corporations and individuals (such as The Paraffine Companies, Kodak Japan, and insurance claimants) attempting to remit earnings or liquidate capital from Japan. The file covers Japanese financial diplomacy across the yen bloc, French Indochina, the Netherlands East Indies, and South America, culminating in the bilateral freezing of assets in July 1941. Subsequent entries index reports on Japanese financial ordinances, the financial surveillance of American firms in Tokyo, FBI reports on covert cash withdrawals by Japanese diplomatic missions in the United States, and intelligence collected by the Coordinator of Information on capital flight and gold movements prior to the outbreak of war.

subfiles.about: Department of State docket sheet recording correspondence regarding foreign exchange remittances from Japan for the Bates International Bag Company.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet (Form DS-46) indexes correspondence from January 1940 regarding the remittance of funds from Japan by the Bates International Bag Company. The Department of State noted that the remittance situation had not materially changed. It advised that the American Embassy in Tokyo stood under standing instructions to assist American commercial interests upon presentation of relevant facts.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers, Form DS-46 (Sub No. 190)

subfiles.about: Department of State docket sheet indexing documents on Japanese exchange resources, trade on open account, and corporate liquidation from January to August 1940.
subfiles.summary: Sheet #27 indexes nine entries concerning Japan's foreign exchange position, the adverse impact of the depreciating British pound on Japanese imports and exports, and the application of exchange controls to American travelers. It tracks discussions on the advisability of open-account shipments to Japan and records the efforts of The Paraffine Companies, Inc. to negotiate the sale of its equity in Sakuma Co., Ltd. to Japanese stockholders demanding payment in American currency. Notable officials referenced include Herbert Feis, George F. Luthringer, George A. Makinson, and Ambassador Joseph C. Grew.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers, Sheet #27 (Sub Nos. 191-199)

subfiles.about: Continuous seven-page docket register recording diplomatic, intelligence, and commercial papers concerning Japanese exchange controls, asset freezing, and global financial operations from late 1940 to early 1942.
subfiles.summary: This sequential seven-page docket list (Sheets 31 through 37) indexes communications from November 1940 to March 1942 documenting the escalation of financial conflict between the United States and Japan. It details American corporate struggles to liquidate assets and remit funds (including Paraffine Companies, Kodak Japan, and insurance firms), currency negotiations with the Banque de l'Indochine, and Japanese banking maneuvers in the Netherlands East Indies and Latin America (Peru, Brazil, Bolivia, and Chile). Following the July 1941 asset freeze, entries record Japanese exchange control ordinances, inspections of American corporate assets in Tokyo, FBI reports on large cash withdrawals by Japanese diplomatic and military personnel in the United States, and intelligence gathered by the Coordinator of Information on capital flight and gold shipments prior to the outbreak of war.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers, Sheets #31-37 (Sub Nos. 218-272)
